Professor Alderman set down his coffee and regarded the student across from him.

"You want to know how it's actually done," he said. It wasn't a question.

The student — brilliant, reckless, burning with the specific ambition of someone who has nothing left to lose — nodded.

"I spent fourteen years in pharmaceutical chemistry," Alderman said. "I know the synthesis process for a dozen controlled substances better than I know my own address. "Yes," said the student.

Alderman was quiet for a long moment.

"MDMA," he said finally. "We'll start there."
